title: Keep deployment activity and cost evidence together

scenes.title: Keep deployment activity and cost evidence together
scenes.narration: Welcome to Resgrid Academy. In this lesson, we will keep deployment activity and cost evidence together. Extended mutual-aid work needs clear personnel, apparatus, dates, and cost records that can be reviewed after demobilization. We will explain the features, the setup decisions, and a practical way to check the result.

scenes.title: A department scenario
scenes.narration: A strike-team deployment is recorded with its personnel, apparatus and dates. Keep deployment records and cost documentation together for review and reimbursement. The examples in this series use a fictional department and are teaching scenarios, not default settings.

scenes.title: Deployment Finance
scenes.narration: Deployment Finance. Deployment records and Deployment Finance. Record your next deployment with its personnel and apparatus.

scenes.title: New Deployment
scenes.narration: New Deployment. Start a deployment record. Useful when your members deploy to incidents outside your jurisdiction.

scenes.title: Deployment From External Order
scenes.narration: Deployment From External Order. Create a deployment from a mutual-aid resource order. Useful when your members deploy to incidents outside your jurisdiction.

scenes.title: Mutual-aid resource orders
scenes.narration: Resource orders describe requested resources and the fills departments offer or accept. Review ordering settings and participating departments. Create a fictional request, offer a fill, and review acceptance. Reconcile requested quantities, accepted fills, and the remaining resource need. Confirm availability in the demo department before recording the live workflow.

scenes.title: External orders and deployment closeout
scenes.narration: An external order records the department fills and their mobilization, release, and actual return home. Enter an approved sample external order, link its deployment, record the fill transitions, and complete closeout. Review dates and resource identity. This workspace records manual entry and artifact snapshots; it is not an external ordering connector. Confirm availability in the demo department before recording the live workflow.

scenes.title: Deployment time and export reports
scenes.narration: Read-only deployment reports bring time entries, supporting artifacts, and export outputs together. Open a recorded demo deployment and review its time report, summary, and available exports. Reconcile each time entry with the roster and recorded dates before finance review. Confirm availability in the demo department before recording the live workflow.

scenes.title: Configure one useful workflow
scenes.narration: For the training scenario, work in this order. Step 1. Create a deployment or start from an external resource order. Step 2. Identify the assigned personnel, apparatus, and operational dates. Step 3. Record deployment activity and finance documentation for review.

scenes.title: Verify the result
scenes.narration: Now verify the result. Reconcile the deployment resources and dates with supporting records. Review any daily time and cost documentation required by the workflow. A common problem to watch for: Deployment Finance is separate from the Business Operations add-on. A prepared record does not guarantee reimbursement.

scenes.title: Try it with your department
scenes.narration: Your practice task is simple. Record a two-day demo strike-team deployment and reconcile the participating people and units with the supporting documents. Record the result, who owns the follow-up, and when it should be reviewed. Use the linked feature scripts for the detailed screen recording plan.
